h1: Outdoor Playground Equipment Manufacturer & Supplier in Asansol

h1Text: Outdoor Playground Equipment Manufacturer & Supplier in Asansol

items.pText: Asansol is a coal, steel and railway town, and many of its parks belong to industrial and railway townships laid out decades ago. A lot of the play equipment in those parks is old painted steel that has rusted or broken. FunPlay Systems manufactures replacement outdoor playground equipment for Asansol's township parks, schools, housing complexes and clubs. We make it at our factory in Vasai, about 1,530 km away, and send it by road for installation by our team or a dealer.

Replacing an old playground is a different job from building a new one. The existing footings, paths and trees are already there, and the new layout has to work with them. Old concrete bases rarely match new equipment, so we usually suggest breaking them out and grouting fresh ones. Asansol's summers are very hot and the monsoon is heavy, and coal dust settles on everything in parts of the town. Galvanised steel and roto-moulded plastic can be washed down and will not rust under the grime.

richText.heading: Replacing old playground equipment in township parks

c: Start by photographing the park as it is, including old bases, trees, lights and paths. Mark anything that must stay. We then suggest new pieces and send a layout drawing that fits around them, with safe play areas that do not run into tree trunks or benches.
Remove old equipment fully, including buried stumps of posts, before new installation begins. A

items.q: Can you replace old rusted equipment in our township park?
items.a: Yes. Send us photos of the park and the old equipment. We suggest new pieces and a layout that works around existing trees and paths, and our team or a dealer installs them.

items.q: Can new equipment use the old concrete bases?
items.a: Usually not, because old footings rarely match new posts. We generally suggest removing them and grouting fresh bases. We confirm this once we see the site.

items.q: How do we clean equipment in a dusty industrial area?
items.a: Wash it down with water and a soft brush. Galvanised steel and roto-moulded plastic do not rust, so regular washing keeps them clean without harming the surface.
